editorial:
If you grew up watching Naruto, this movie feels like a warm reunion with a fresh twist. Boruto Uzumaki is a talented young ninja who has his dad's fire but none of his patience. The problem is that Naruto, now the Seventh Hokage, is always buried in paperwork and village duties, leaving Boruto feeling ignored. When Boruto meets Sasuke, he begs to become his apprentice, hoping to prove he can stand on his own. The story mixes family drama with big ninja action, and it never takes itself too seriously.

The animation looks sharp, especially during the fight scenes, and the voice acting carries real emotion. The pacing moves quickly, though some side characters get pushed aside. Fans of the original series will love the callbacks, while newcomers might feel a little lost. Still, the heart of the story is easy to follow. If you want the best experience, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Momoshiki absorbs Naruto's power and tries to destroy the village. Boruto, with help from Sasuke and a Rasengan from his father, lands the finishing blow. Afterward, Boruto finally understands why his dad works so hard, and the two share a heartfelt moment. Naruto gives Boruto his old headband, and Boruto promises to keep growing as a ninja and as a son.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action-packed anime with strong family themes.
